key_findings: CORE VERDICT: WITHIN the eligibility horizon, local recurrent credit (e-prop = RFLO = the diagonal/SnAp-1 truncation of RTRL) is essentially BPTT-competitive (within a few % of BPTT); BEYOND the horizon it structurally loses credit unless the net carries far context in SLOW neuron states (ALIF) or in INDEPENDENT/near-linear recurrent modules. Exactly the shape the project measured: modest within-reach gain, no credit past ~1/alpha, drift beyond.

e-prop (Bellec 2020, Nature Comms/bioRxiv 738385): on TIMIT phoneme recognition e-prop is 'competitive with BPTT for both LSTM and spiking LSNN; error rate only a few percent larger than the BPTT baseline in all cases, even when feedback weights are random.' Paper reports curves not tables (honest: within a few pts). Concrete pinned datapoint: e-prop 91.12% on Google Speech Commands GSC-12 (Frontiers e-prop-on-SpiNNaker2), matching BPTT-SNN baselines.

ALIF is the single most important lever and the reason e-prop matches BPTT on temporal tasks: adaptive-threshold neurons have a slow hidden variable whose eligibility 'propagates forward over longer time spans' -- Bellec's 'highways into the future,' enabling credit across delays >2s that plain LIF cannot. Without ALIF, forward eligibility decays in ~1/alpha steps and deep credit is absent (matches project alpha=0.3 -> ~3-token reach, none past d10).

RFLO (Murray 2019, eLife): the rate twin of e-prop; cleanest boundary statement -- RFLO 'works about as well as full-gradient BPTT/RTRL when task timescale is short; where timescales are longer, RFLO struggles versus BPTT.'

e-prop and RFLO are the SAME diagonal RTRL truncation (Taxonomy of Recurrent Learning Rules, arXiv 2207.11439/JMLR 19-562): keep only per-synapse forward-filtered eligibility, drop the recurrent-Jacobian off-diagonal (cross-neuron) sensitivity. Credit routed THROUGH recurrent mixing (not a single neuron's slow state) is lost -- the structural cause of the deep-context shortfall.

LM evidence at moderate scale is favorable: SnAp (Menick 2020, arXiv 2006.07232), the online sparse-RTRL family containing e-prop as SnAp-1, on char-level WikiText-103 with sparse GRUs 'closely matches the gold-standard accuracy of a BPTT-trained model' (SnAp-2 slightly>SnAp-1; 99.9%-sparse 4096-unit -> 1.38 bpc). SnAp-2/3 'mostly outperform or match BPTT' fully-online (T=1) where truncated-BPTT 'completely fails to learn long-term structure.'

Long-range gap-closer -- Zucchet 2023 (NeurIPS, arXiv 2305.15947): online RTRL becomes 'competitive with offline BPTT on Long Range Arena' via INDEPENDENT/diagonal recurrent modules (linear-RNN/LRU). Lesson: online learning CAN match BPTT long-range, but the lever is ARCHITECTURE (independent/near-linear recurrence + multi-layer), not the local rule. Same paper: SnAp-1 diagonal bias HURTS MORE on linear RNNs.

RANDOM vs SYMMETRIC feedback: random (feedback alignment) costs only a few % vs symmetric on e-prop (Bellec) AND is the more STABLE arm at LM scale -- project found symmetric/weight-transport DESTABILIZES (W_out<->W_rec runaway, agg +0.233, 0/6) while fixed-random B is robust (a point FOR biology). For DEEP stacks, learned feedback (Kolen-Pollack) fixes cross-layer alignment.

PROJECT RATE RESULT (2026-07-11-eprop-REAL-WITH-SCOPE) is fully consistent: random-feedback e-prop on W_rec recovers within-horizon context 6/6 (deep-bucket win ~-0.04 to -0.06 nats, dose-dependent, shuffle-control kills it -> genuine credit-structure), but stable regularized magnitude MODEST, raw capacity comparable-or-stronger here, NO credit beyond ~1/alpha (unregularized W_rec drifts, tamed by weight decay).

PROJECT SPIKING RESULT (2026-07-11-onbridge-BDSP): on-bridge BDSP/Burstprop validates the credit MECHANISM 6/6 (clean, dominant 4-7x over drift, burst-coupled via bdsp_apical_couples_soma, no weight transport) but the CE-improvement is SEED-VARIABLE (plastic beats fixed 2/6, mean ~neutral) because burst-multiplexed feedback-alignment is COARSER than rate RFLO. Rate e-prop's clean within-reach recovery only partially transfers to spikes at cheap scale.
researchOut.mechanism_detail: Why the short/long split is structural: BPTT computes the exact gradient by propagating error backward through the full recurrent Jacobian product. RTRL computes the same forward but carries a rank-3 sensitivity tensor dh/dW (O(n^3-n^4)). e-prop and RFLO are the SAME cheap truncation: keep only the DIAGONAL of that sensitivity (per-synapse forward-filtered eligibility e[j,i]=low-pass of psi_j*h_pre_i) times a broadcast/random-projected instantaneous error L=B@delta. This is exactly SnAp-1. The dropped off-diagonal terms are the credit flowing through OTHER neurons over time, so any dependency stored in the RECURRENT MIXING (distributed dynamics) is invisible, while any dependency stored in a SINGLE unit's slowly-decaying state IS visible. Hence (a) ALIF adaptive neurons turn long-range memory into a single-unit slow state the diagonal eligibility can track, and (b) diagonal/linear-RNN architectures (Zucchet) close the gap by construction -- if recurrence is diagonal, the diagonal sensitivity is EXACT, so online==offline. The eligibility time constant sets a hard credit horizon ~1/(1-decay); beyond it the update is unbiased-but-uninformative perturbation that unregularized drifts (project d10+ +0.52 blowup, tamed to -0.05 by weight decay). Random vs symmetric feedback affects only alignment, not the horizon -- random costs a few % and is more stable (no transport runaway). Richer factorizations (SnAp-2/3, k-step recurrent influence) interpolate toward RTRL/BPTT at k-fold cost and recover longer dependencies. Net: the local rule is BPTT-equivalent up to its eligibility horizon and structurally blind past it; every gap-closer works by EXTENDING that horizon -- slow neuron states (ALIF), architecture making the diagonal exact (LRU/independent modules), or a less-diagonal sensitivity (SnAp-2). Kolen-Pollack learned feedback separately fixes cross-LAYER (spatial) alignment in deep stacks, orthogonal to the temporal horizon.
researchOut.expected_fraction_of_bptt: Plain multi-layer RATE recurrent LM at TinyStories scale (23.7M tok, V=2000, block 128) targeting the full-backprop LSTM depth margin (ctx1 +0.5 -> ctx17-128 +1.8 nats over bigram): roughly 0.5-0.7 of BPTT's TOTAL depth-margin, HIGHLY depth-dependent. Near-parity (~0.85-1.0 of BPTT) at shallow/mid depth (ctx1 to ~ctx8, within the eligibility horizon; SnAp-1/e-prop reaches BPTT there, SnAp-2 matches fully), but only ~0.2-0.4 of BPTT's DEEP asymptote (ctx17-128) with vanilla LIF/tanh eligibility -- that tail is the beyond-horizon credit e-prop cannot assign. researchOut.mechanism_detail: There are TWO ORTHOGONAL credit axes and the project has validated them separately, never jointly, and the on-substrate join is where the residual gap lives. AXIS 1 = SPATIAL/DEPTH credit (layer l+1 -> layer l), which is Burstprop's job: a pyramidal ensemble multiplexes event-rate E (feedforward, basal-driven) and burst-probability P (top-down credit, apical-driven), B=P*E; the descending burst-coded error v_api,l = Y_l*(b_{l+1}-baseline) sets P_l which drives BDSP dw = eta*(B-Pbar*E)*Etilde_pre (Payeur 2021 M1.1-M1.5; spec in 2026-07-01-burst-multiplexed-...-spec.md). This is IMPLEMENTED in sim/bridge.py and works at rate to depth-2, is depth-fragile at depth-3. AXIS 2 = TEMPORAL credit (token t-k -> token t), which is e-prop/RFLO's job (Bellec 2020 = Murray 2019): a forward-filtered eligibility trace e[j,i] = (1-a)e + psi_j*h_prev carries past activity, and the SAME broadcast learning signal L=B@delta credits W_rec online with NO BPTT. The external literature is explicit that these are DIFFERENT axes: e-prop does temporal-credit-well but uses random-feedback/broadcast for the spatial (layer) part (OSTL/e-prop separate spatial vs temporal). Burstprop does spatial-depth-credit; it is NOT a temporal-sequence rule by itself. The scale-validated target (+1.8 nats growing to context depth 128) needs a MULTI-LAYER RECURRENT net = BOTH axes at once, over many tokens, ON SPIKES. What is proven: (i) the BDSP rule and its multiplexing are on-substrate and byte-safe; (ii) axis-1 works at rate depth-2 (emerge1b GO), is fragile at depth-3, and depth-stability is unsolved; (iii) axis-2 works at rate SINGLE-layer within a ~3-token eligibility horizon (MODEST), and drifts beyond it; (iv) on real spikes the recurrent credit machinery is clean/dominant/6-6 but the CE-win is seed-variable because burst-multiplexed FA is a coarser gradient than the rate RFLO, AND because RS Izhikevich neurons need the apical-soma coupling edit to burst at all. The RESIDUAL GAP to a multi-layer recurrent sequence net is therefore FOUR concrete deficits, none yet closed: (a) DEPTH-STABILITY past 2 layers (D2 unsolved even at rate); (b) TEMPORAL credit BEYOND the ~1/alpha eligibility horizon (nothing reaches d10+ yet - a stable ALIF/adaptive-threshold horizon extension is the named-but-unbuilt lever); (c) the rate->spike COARSENESS of burst-multiplexed FA (graded burst-fraction read untested); (d) MULTI-LAYER + RECURRENT jointly (the reuse base is a SINGLE recurrent layer; deep-x-recurrent-x-spiking is the acknowledged field-wide open problem, the D3 target). This is precisely the 'e-prop for time x feedback-alignment for layers at once' mechanism the fork calls for, and it directly extends your single-layer reuse base.

THE FRAGILITY IS TWO-FOLD AND MULTIPLICATIVE for a deep recurrent net. (1) TEMPORAL: e-prop is a DIAGONAL (RTRL) approximation -- it forward-accumulates the on-diagonal sensitivity and DROPS off-diagonal cross-neuron terms, so genuinely long-range temporal dependence beyond the eligibility horizon is truncated (your own grad_check already shows this: cos to full-gradient degrades at spectral 1.1, recovers at 0.2). (2) SPATIAL: vanilla feedback alignment / DFA is documented to DEGRADE WITH DEPTH and to FAIL on hard/deep tasks (CIFAR-100/ImageNet, conv nets). Stacking recurrent layers adds a spatial credit path ON TOP of the temporal one, so both must succeed at once -- the depth path is the NEW fragility your single-layer runner never exercised.

ROOT CAUSE OF FA DEPTH-FRAGILITY IS WELL CHARACTERIZED AND HAS CHEAP FIXES. Two named mechanisms: (a) NORM MISMATCH -- fixed feedback B stays constant while forward weights W grow during training, so the B/W norm ratio drives vanishing/exploding learning signals with depth; (b) RANK COLLAPSE -- the feedback pathway converges to low rank, worsening with depth ('Overcoming Rank Collapse in Feedback Alignment', arXiv:2606.11123, 2026). The rank-collapse paper's FIX is cheap: INJECT NOISE into the feedback weights each step to preserve full rank; it enables training where vanilla FA completely fails at depth, and the noise strategy generalizes across architectures (incl. recurrent).

LEARNED FEEDBACK is the single highest-leverage upgrade over fixed-random B and is CHEAP + biologically legal (no weight transport). Kolen-Pollack / weight-mirror rules (Akrout et al. 2019, 'Deep Learning without Weight Transport') update B by a LOCAL symmetric rule so it ALIGNS to the forward inter-layer weights, directly curing the FA depth-degradation + rank-collapse the fixed random matrix suffers. Your runner already has the 'symmetric' (W_out^T, transport ceiling) arm -- learned KP feedback is the biologically-legal middle rung between fixed-random and symmetric, ~10 lines.

PREDICTIVE CODING NOW SCALES TO DEPTH but is EXPENSIVE per step. muPC (arXiv:2505.13124, NeurIPS 2025) uses a Depth-muP reparameterization to stably train 100+ layer (up to 128) predictive-coding nets with zero-shot LR transfer across width AND depth -- solving the exact 'PC/EqProp notoriously can't train very deep nets' problem. BUT PC requires ITERATIVE equilibrium inference (many relaxation steps per input) and is non-causal for a streaming LM, so it is the depth-ROBUST FALLBACK, not a cheap first move. EqProp is even worse-matched: two-phase energy-based equilibrium, non-causal; recent scaling work (bias-cancellation, holomorphic EP exact gradients, intermediate error signals for deep conv CRNNs arXiv:2508.15989) is real but still equilibrium/offline -- deprioritize for a causal streaming LM.

THE SPIKING LAYER-CREDIT ANSWER YOU ALREADY OWN IS BURSTPROP/BDSP. Payeur-Guerguiev-Zenke-Richards-Naud (Nature Neuroscience 2021) 'Burst-dependent synaptic plasticity can coordinate learning in hierarchical circuits' carries the TOP-DOWN teaching signal DOWN the layer hierarchy via burst-rate MULTIPLEXING -- an online, local, spike-based multi-layer credit rule that trains ImageNet (~56% top-5). This IS the spatial(layer) credit; combine it with e-prop eligibility for the temporal axis. It is already partly in sim/bridge.py (enable_bdsp, cp_bdsp_apical_drive, fused_bdsp_update) -> the biology-faithful end target once the rate-level multi-layer test is GO.

OTHER CHEAP LOCAL-DEPTH OPTIONS (weaker, sanity-floor tier): DRTP (Frenkel-Lefebvre 2019, 'Direct Random Target Projection') projects the TARGET (not the error) through a fixed random matrix directly to each layer -- purely feedforward, no feedback path, no update-locking, cheapest possible depth credit but weakest (near-BP only on MNIST/CIFAR-10). TESS (arXiv:2502.01837, 2025) is a scalable TEMPORALLY-AND-SPATIALLY-local rule for SNNs (both axes local at once). Forward-DFA (arXiv:2403.08804) gives online gradient estimates of SNNs via forward direct feedback alignment. These bound the cheap end but are unlikely to beat learned-feedback deep-e-prop on an LM.
researchOut.mechanism_detail:
e-prop already FACTORIZES the gradient as dL/dW_ji = (learning signal L_j) x (eligibility trace e_ji). The eligibility e_ji is FORWARD-accumulated and purely local -> it handles the TIME axis (and its horizon is set by the leak/ALIF adaptation, your existing lever). The learning signal L_j carries the INSTANTANEOUS/SPATIAL credit -- 'how does unit j's activity change the loss right now.' For a SINGLE layer, L_j = (B @ delta)_j with delta the readout error and B a fixed random feedback (broadcast alignment). MULTI-LAYER is exactly where the new fragility lives: each hidden layer ell needs its OWN L^ell that reflects how that layer's activity affects the loss THROUGH the layers above it. There are two ways to supply it, and this is the crux of 'credit across time AND layers at once':

(A) DIRECT BROADCAST across depth (DFA-style, cheapest): each layer gets L^ell = B_ell @ delta directly from the OUTPUT error via its own fixed random matrix. One matrix per layer, no propagation. This is the naive multi-layer e-prop. It is what DEGRADES WITH DEPTH -- a single random projection cannot convey layer-specific credit; norm mismatch + rank collapse bite. Test this FIRST as the fragility probe.

This yields the SAME table shape the ceiling prints.

=== 3. BATCHING OVER CONTIGUOUS BLOCKS ===
Training uses the ceiling's `stateful_batches` lane structure: split `tr` into `batch` contiguous lanes `base=(bs,lane)`, iterate consecutive 128-blocks j=0..nb-1, `is_start = (j==0)`. Primary config = BLOCK-MATCHED e-prop: at each block start reset (h, eligibility e, adaptation ad) per lane so the credit horizon is <=128, exactly matching the ceiling's block-matched LSTM (fresh state per block, BPTT-within-128). This makes 'does e-prop-within-128 capture what BPTT-within-128 captures' the clean question. A `--stateful` flag (mirrors the ceiling) carries (h,e,ad) ACROSS blocks within a lane (never reset) = the biologically-faithful unbounded-eligibility mode and a follow-on lever (does horizon beyond 128 help?). The whole per-lane state is a batched tensor: h (bs,n) per layer, e (bs,n,n) per layer, ad (bs,n) per layer.

=== 4. THE RATE E-PROP FORWARD+UPDATE (torch/cupy, batched over lanes) ===
Port the runner's `train()`/`_train_alif()` equations to a batched GPU tensor form (dtype fp32). Per token t in a block, per layer l=1..L (h^0_t = W_in @ x_t, the fixed-random input projection = the ESN invariant; optionally plastic):
  pre^l = h^{l-1}_t @ W_ff^l.T + h^l_{t-1} @ W_rec^l.T + b^l   [ - beta*ad^l if ALIF]
  act^l = tanh(pre^l);  h^l_t = (1-a^l)*h^l_{t-1} + a^l*act^l
  logits = h^L_t @ W_out.T;  p = softmax(logits);  delta = onehot(target) - p   (clean local next-token error, no BPTT)
  READ-OUT (delta rule, batched, summed over lanes): W_out += lr_out*(mean_lane outer(delta, h^L_t) - wd*W_out)
  psi^l = a^l * (1 - act^l**2)   (pseudo-derivative)
  ELIGIBILITY (forward-filtered, per weight; batched (bs,n,n)):
    recurrent: e^l_rec = (1-a^l)*e^l_rec + psi^l[:, :,None]*h^l_{t-1}[:, None,:]
    feedforward (reads layer below): e^l_ff = (1-a^l)*e^l_ff + psi^l[:, :,None]*h^{l-1}_t[:, None,:]
    (ALIF layers use the runner's VALIDATED 2-component coupled recursion eps_a/eps_h — carry it verbatim.)
  LEARNING SIGNAL per layer = DIRECT FEEDBACK ALIGNMENT (fixed random B^l, n_l×V, NO weight transport):
    L^l = delta @ B^l.T
  W_rec^l += lr_rec*(mean_lane L^l[:, :,None]*e^l_rec - wd_rec*W_rec^l)
  W_ff^l  += lr_ff *(mean_lane L^l[:, :,None]*e^l_ff)
  (symmetric-feedback ceiling: L^l = delta @ W_out for the top layer / propagate via W_ff^T for lower layers — the within-net weight-transport bound; shuffle-B control: permute B^l once.)
All updates are torch.no_grad() local rules — e-prop is NOT autograd. The read-out is trained over the WHOLE stream (streaming delta at every position). Input W_in fixed-random by default (ESN); a `--plastic-input` flag trains it from L^1 by the same eligibility on the embedding.

L stacked leaky-tanh recurrent layers (DeepESN topology, Gallicchio-Micheli: unidirectional, higher layers slower/less-contractive — assign a slower leak spectrum to higher layers so depth ALSO buys longer timescales). Feedforward W_ff^l carries h^{l-1}->layer l; recurrent W_rec^l is within-layer. Credit is DFA: each layer's own fixed-random B^l @ delta — no error is propagated DOWN through W_ff^T (that would be backprop/weight-transport).
